newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal debt body signals rates could fall.
newsitem.headline: Portugal debt body signals rates could fall.

text.p: Portugal's public debt manager, the Institute for Public Credit Management (IGCP), gave two clear signals on Wednesday that it expects domestic interest rates to fall, analysts said.

Its rejection of all bids at a three-month Treasury bill sale was followed by the announcement of a 10 billion yen dual-currency loan which IGCP president Vitor Bento told Reuters had been obtained at better conditions than offered by the local market.

Some analysts said that even if the Bank of Portugal sticks to its traditionally cautious line on rates, domestic banks might have to become more aggressive in their bidding at the Treasury bill sales.
"This is a signal, amongst others, that we could already have lower official rates," said Banco Finantia analyst Isabel Costa.

"The state has a wide range of alternatives for its financing. It sees the central bank rates as being high and decides to look abroad. It is logical and it could continue to happen," said an analyst with one foreign bank.

"It means that in the Treasury bill sales, the bids are going to have to become more aggressive because if not, (the IGCP) is going to prefer to issue foreign bonds on favourable terms," said Ana Paula Carvalho of Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI).
With both Portugal and Spain seemingly on course for the European Union's single currency, there was little justification for the relatively wide rate gap between the two, analysts said.
The last six-month and 12-month Treasury bills sold in Portugal were at 5.3445 percent and 5.2823 percent, respectively, against 5.001 and 4.960 percent in Spain.
The Bank of Portugal repo rate stands at 5.70 percent against 5.25 percent in Spain.
